title.ja: 詰将棋の遊び方、ルール

intro.ja:
詰将棋は攻方が最初に指し、毎回王手を続けて玉方を詰ませる問題です。三手詰は攻方、玉方、攻方の合計三手で、攻方の手だけを数えるわけではありません。駒の動き、成り、二歩、打ち歩詰めなどは指し将棋と同じです。一つの逃げ方だけでなく、すべての合法的な応手を読んで詰みを確認します。

玉方は最長になる応手を選び、盤上と攻方の持ち駒にない残りの駒を合駒などに使えます。通常の駒総数を超えることはありません。取られても局面を変えず詰みを先延ばしするだけの無駄合いは、詰将棋では手数に数えません。攻方の駒取りで得た持ち駒も使えます。まず一手詰で逃げ道と王手駒の守りを確かめます。
intro.en:
Tsume-shogi starts with the attacker, who must give check on every attacking turn until mate. A three-move problem counts attacker, defender, attacker: both sides’ moves contribute. Normal movement, promotion, nifu, and pawn-drop-mate restrictions still apply. Finding one cooperative variation is not a solution; every legal defense must be met with a mating continuation, including captures, king moves, and useful interpositions.

The defender chooses a longest resistance and may use pieces not on the board or in the attacker’s hand, within the normal piece inventory. Futile interpositions that only delay an unchanged mate are excluded by tsume convention; useful blocks must be examined. Captures can supply the attacker with new material. Begin with mate-in-one patterns and explicitly test escape squares and protection of the checking piece.

question.ja: 三手詰の解答で玉の一つの逃げ方だけを詰ませれば十分ですか？
question.en: Is mating after one possible king escape enough to solve a three-move problem?

answer.ja: 不十分です。他の逃げ方、王手駒の取り方、合駒にも詰みが続くことを確認します。
answer.en: No. Every legal king move, capture, and useful block must also lead to mate.

courses.title: 詰将棋の遊び方、ルール: 図1-1 詰将棋の一例 → 図1-2 2回王手をかけて詰んだ
courses.titleEn: Tsume-shogi rules: Figure 1-1: Example of a tsume shogi problem → Figure 1-2: Checkmate with two checks
courses.goalFormation:

原図に描かれた駒だけを置いています。

child.commentEn:
Figure 1-2: Checkmate with two checks
The attacker gave repeated checks with a gold in hand and mated. Finding this sequence solves the problem. The defender fled with △2一玉 on the second move, but △3一玉, △4一玉 and others are possible too, and there is a mate against every escape. A problem is solved only when you confirm a mate against any defence.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

section.ja: 攻方は連続で王手して玉方を詰ませる手順を考える
section.en: The attacker plans a sequence of consecutive checks to checkmate the defender

root.comment:
図1-1 詰将棋の一例
図1-1は詰将棋の例です。詰将棋は玉のある「玉方」と玉のない「攻方」に分かれ、攻方から玉方の玉を詰ませる手順を考えるもので、必ず攻方から指します。盤の一部の駒だけを使い、駒の動かし方や二歩、打ち歩詰めなどの基本ルールは通常の将棋と同じです。攻方は常に王手をかけ、玉方は逃げます。
原図に描かれた駒だけを置いています。
root.commentEn:
Figure 1-1: Example of a tsume shogi problem
Figure 1-1 is an example of a tsume-shogi (checkmate problem). The sides are the defender (玉方), who has the king, and the attacker (攻方), who has none; you find a sequence in which the attacker mates, and the attacker always moves first. Only some pieces on the board are used, and basic rules such as piece movement, nifu and uchifuzume are the same as normal shogi. The attacker must give check on every move and the defender runs.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

section.ja: 攻方と玉方に分かれ、玉方を詰ますことを目指す
section.en: Split into attacker and defender, and aim to checkmate the defender

root.commentEn:
Figure 2-1: Example of a one-move tsume shogi problem
Some tsume problems are mate in one and others need many checks. The move count is the total of the attacker's and defender's moves. Consider Figure 2-1.

child.commentEn:
Figure 2-4: Checkmate in seven moves
From Figure 2-3 mate comes after seven moves, so it is a mate in 7. Note that the count includes the defender's moves as well as the attacker's checks. A tsume problem starts and ends with an attacker move, so the move count is always odd.

図3-1 何手で詰む？
詰将棋のルールの一つに、玉方は最長手順になるように逃げなければならない、というものがあります。図3-1を解きながら、玉方の逃げ方を考えてみましょう。何手詰か考えてみてください。

root.commentEn:
Figure 3-1: How many moves to checkmate?
One rule of tsume-shogi is that the defender must flee so that the sequence is longest. Let us consider the defender's escapes while solving Figure 3-1, and think about how many moves it takes.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

child.commentEn:
Figure 4-3: Three-move mate using the knight in hand
Finally, checking with a knight in hand finishes it as a mate in 3. Though any pieces in hand may be used, you cannot use more than normal shogi allows, such as three rooks. The basic rules are those of ordinary shogi.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

child.commentEn:
Figure 5-4: A futile interposition can prolong the sequence
If futile interpositions were continued, Figure 5-1 would become a mate in 15, but such sequences are forbidden in tsume-shogi. Once you know the rules, try beginner mate-in-1 problems.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

section.en: Do not make a wasted interposition

child.comment:
図5-3 無駄な合駒の例 詰将棋では禁止
たとえば図5-2から△1八歩と合駒すれば手数を稼げますが、これは王手している香車でそのまま取れてしまいます。このように攻方が王手している駒でそのまま取れる合駒を、無駄な合駒と考えます。
原図に描かれた駒だけを置いています。
child.commentEn:
Figure 5-3: Example of a futile interposition, prohibited in tsume shogi
For example, interposing △1八歩 in Figure 5-2 would gain moves, but the checking lance can simply capture it. An interposition that the attacker can capture with the checking piece itself is regarded as futile.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

section.en: Do not make a wasted interposition

child.comment:
図5-2 玉方は逃げ道がないが…
図5-1からは▲2六桂と桂馬を退かして王手します。玉方は合駒をすれば粘れそうですが、ここでの合駒は無駄な合駒になります。無駄な合駒は禁止なので、図5-2で詰んでいるとみなし、図5-1は1手詰の詰将棋になります。
原図に描かれた駒だけを置いています。
child.commentEn:
Figure 5-2: The king has no escape, but...
In Figure 5-1, ▲2六桂 moves the knight away to give check. The defender seems able to hold out by interposing, but that interposition would be futile. Since futile interpositions are forbidden, Figure 5-2 counts as mate, and Figure 5-1 is a mate in 1.
Only the pieces drawn in the source figure are placed.

section.en: Do not make a wasted interposition
